gran-habano--corojo-no-5.description: Gran Habano's Corojo No. 5 is rolled in Honduras by the Rico family, with a dark, reddish Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper over long filler from Nicaragua and Costa Rica. The company presents it as the strongest blend in its range. The smoke rests on pecan, chocolate and warm baking spice, with a floral edge on the retrohale; one for an unhurried evening.

thirds.notes: Pecan and chocolate open, with ginger and allspice on the finish and a floral note through the nose.
The chocolate recedes and pecan takes the lead, while ginger and allspice keep the palate lively.
Wood joins the pecan, a trace of chocolate returns, and the floral retrohale holds to the end.

gran-habano--connecticut-no-1.description: Gran Habano's Connecticut No. 1 pairs an Ecuadorian Connecticut wrapper with Nicaraguan binder and filler, rolled at the Rico family's operation in Honduras. It smokes mild to medium: smooth and creamy with a nutty core at first, then a slowly building coffee note and leather through the second half. A gentle companion for a morning coffee.

thirds.notes: Smooth and creamy with a nutty core; a hint of coffee gathers towards the middle.
Leather moves to the front as the coffee note keeps growing.
Leather stays dominant, with a faint touch of spice tucked underneath.

sources.title: Cigar Place – Gran Habano Connecticut #1 review
Cigar World – Gran Habano Connecticut No. 1 review

gran-habano--habano-no-3.description: Made by Gran Habano at GR Tabacaleras Unidas in Honduras, the Habano No. 3 wraps a sheeny Nicaraguan Habano leaf around a Nicaraguan binder and long filler from Nicaragua, Costa Rica and Mexico. Cedar, leather and a dense, unsweetened cream lead, joined by nutmeg-like baking spice and, late in the smoke, black pepper.

thirds.notes: Leather and cedar first, then a dense cream and nutmeg-style baking spice settle in.
The cream deepens, a caramel-like sweetness appears, and the spice turns nuttier and woodier.
Black pepper finally arrives and leather returns as the flavors grow quieter.

sources.title: Cigar Dojo – Gran Habano Habano #3 Rothschild review
Best Cigar Prices – Gran Habano Habano #3 Gran Robusto review

gran-habano--vintage-2002.description: The Vintage 2002 builds on Gran Habano's Corojo No. 5 blend with a dark, oily Nicaraguan Corojo wrapper from 2002, rolled at the family's GR Tabacaleras factory in Honduras. It opens with earth, wood and dry toast, gains a light sweetness and spice midway, and closes with cocoa; suited to the end of a good meal.

thirds.notes: Earth and wood with dry toast and sweet tobacco, a faint leathery note, and a draw that turns creamy.
Clove and cayenne-like spice arrive with a hint of vanilla and some sweetness over earth.
Cocoa grows alongside the wood, with a touch of licorice in the sweetness towards the end.
